subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir registered the toxin as a subtle wrongness in how he moved, a falter in the stride of someone who had been pressing a meaningful advantage over Ilvara.
source_quote: I watched the dragonborn's body register the toxin — not a dramatic collapse, nothing so clean as that — just a subtle wrongness in how he moved, a falter in the stride of someone who had been, until thirty seconds ago, pressing a meaningful advantage over Ilvara.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir disengaged and went straight up ten feet, hovering in that particular way of someone who has made the tactically correct decision and is not happy about it.
source_quote: He disengaged and went straight up. Ten feet. Clear of the worst of the cloud, hovering in that particular way of someone who has made the tactically correct decision and is not happy about it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said he was out of actions and bonus actions, and would just kind of look on and be confused.
source_quote: "I'm out of actions and bonus actions," he said, from somewhere above the spore line, "so I guess I'll just kind of look on and be confused."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir felt frustration wearing a physical costume after being poisoned.
source_quote: The poisoned condition settling over a person looks different depending on who they are. On Zalthir it looked like frustration wearing a physical costume.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed the fallen guards had been through quite a lot.
source_quote: Zalthir said, from his aerial vantage point, "Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot."

subject: Valen
fact: Valen could have been one of the repurposed soldiers, and somewhere between then and now, he had lost the thread entirely.
source_quote: Then he reflected on Valen. Not out loud, really — it was more in the quality of the silence that followed. I felt the thought land in the room anyway. Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized. These bodies on the cavern floor had once been exactly what Valen was, and somewhere between then and now, they had lost the thread entirely.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara called up four shapes rising from the cavern floor with the patient, purposeless movement of things that are no longer choosing to move — they are simply directed.
source_quote: And then Ilvara called them up. Four shapes. Rising from the cavern floor with the patient, purposeless movement of things that are no longer choosing to move — they are simply directed.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara's corruption made visible the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence through the repurposed Velkynvelve guards.
source_quote: Former Velkynvelve guards. I recognized the posture of soldiers whose bodies had been repurposed, the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence made visible through Ilvara's particular corruption.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan ran toward the Glyph of Warding on the bridge, distracted and angry enough that he might not be tracking the floor carefully.
source_quote: The Glyph of Warding on the bridge was still live. We'd placed it with exactly this kind of chaos in mind, and Jorlan was close enough, distracted enough, *angry* enough that he might not be tracking the floor carefully.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan ran toward the trap and the glyph detonated.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot," I called across the chaos. He ran toward the trap. The glyph detonated.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan was not having his best moment after the glyph detonated.
source_quote: Jorlan himself was not having his best moment.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator called Jorlan an idiot and invited him toward an explosive ward, betting on ego overriding tactical awareness.
source_quote: "Come get it, idiot," I called across the chaos. ... The tactic had been a gamble — you call a man an idiot and invite him toward an explosive ward and you are making a bet on ego overriding tactical awareness, which is sometimes a safe bet and sometimes gets you killed.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator committed the Dust of Suleiman and cast it directly onto the Big Heart Fungus.
source_quote: I committed the Dust of Suleiman and cast it directly onto the fungus.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz cast a shaped Fireball at fourth level, hitting Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon simultaneously, while sculpting the spell to spare Zalthir and Thorin.
source_quote: Then Daz's shaped Fireball hit — Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon both, simultaneously — and the two effects overlapped in a way that exceeded what either spell would have done alone. ... I carve them out. The fire will know the shape of them by the time it arrives and it will go around — not because fire cares, fire doesn't care about anything, but because I told it the shape of what it cannot touch.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz's Fireball landed exactly where placed, hitting Ilvara and the icon for twelve damage each, while sparing Zalthir and Thorin.
source_quote: The sphere lands where I placed it. Ilvara is quick. She half-saves, which is professionally irritating but not unexpected — she did not survive this long in Menzoberranzan's social ecosystem by being slow. She takes twelve. The icon takes twelve. The fire roars around Zalthir and Thorin and doesn't touch them.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard, and finds purpose in reading the board and identifying highest-value targets.
source_quote: I have found purpose. I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin closed on Jorlan after the glyph detonated, landing a critical Dawnbringer strike for 14 damage.
source_quote: I was already closing on Jorlan. The explosion was still ringing through the cavern when Dawnbringer came down — crit, the blade's light cutting into him hard and clean, 14 damage landing exactly where it needed to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin used the Sap to shove Jorlan off-balance, leaving him on the back foot with disadvantage.
source_quote: I pressed the Sap after it, using the momentum wrong to do something right — shoving him off-balance, leaving him on the back foot, disadvantage waiting for him the next time he tried to hit back.

subject: Thorin
fact: A servant swung at Thorin with a natural 1, then connected for 5 damage — a glancing blow that served as a reminder.
source_quote: One of the servants wasn't finished with me. Legendary action, a swing that went so wide it almost circled back around to being impressive — natural 1, nothing — and then the follow-up connected for 5. Glancing. A reminder.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator noted the specific combination of factors that produced the battlefield shift: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does.
source_quote: I noted the specific combination of factors that had produced that outcome: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator noted that the Big Heart Fungus was still standing, anchoring the far end of the battlefield.
source_quote: The fungus was still standing. The fight was far from over.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator noted that the battlefield had shifted in their favor after the combined spells and tactics.
source_quote: But the battlefield had shifted in our favor, and I noted the specific combination of factors that had produced that outcome: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator took notes on the conditions that made the glyph gamble pay off, in case they became relevant again.
source_quote: I took note of the conditions that made it pay, in case they became relevant again.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator filed away the thought that the difference between soldiers and weapons is sometimes just time and circumstance, and chose not to dwell on it mid-combat.
source_quote: Soldiers. Now weapons. The difference between the two is sometimes just time and circumstance, and I filed that thought away under *things not to dwell on mid-combat*.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum called out, "Come get it, idiot," triggering Jorlan's charge toward the Glyph of Warding.
source_quote: Grygum called out. "Come get it, idiot."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said, "Kaboom," and then, with genuine surprise, "I didn't expect it to work."
source_quote: Grygum said, "Kaboom!" And then, with something like genuine surprise underneath it: "I didn't expect it to work."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum had the idea for the Glyph of Warding, or at least voiced it.
source_quote: The Glyph was Grygum's idea, or at least Grygum's mouth.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan committed to the bridge without hesitation, running toward what he thought was his prize.
source_quote: The drow didn't hesitate, didn't slow — he came across that bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan took the full force of the Glyph of Warding, 21 damage, and was not fast enough to clear it.
source_quote: Jorlan took the full force. He hadn't cleared it in time, hadn't been fast enough, hadn't seen it coming the way you can't see it coming when you're already running at what you think is your prize.

subject: Jorlan
fact: One of the spore servants Jorlan brought across with him came apart completely.
source_quote: Twenty-one damage blooming through the cluster all at once — through the spore servants he'd brought across with him, through Jorlan himself. One servant came apart completely. Just gone.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator calculated Jorlan’s vulnerability to the Glyph in approximately one second, which is about as long as tactical decisions get in a room that is actively trying to kill you.
source_quote: I calculated this in approximately one second, which is about as long as tactical decisions get in a room that is actively trying to kill you.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator believes precision is not the opposite of force — it is force, directed.
source_quote: Precision is not the opposite of force. It is force, directed.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator finds the irony of being the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard almost invisible, even to themselves.
source_quote: The irony is almost invisible, even to me.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator prefers to file things away and not let stakes surface, but the stakes involving Asha keep surfacing.
source_quote: Asha was explicit enough about what's riding on this that I haven't been able to fully file it away the way I prefer to file things. It keeps surfacing.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator observed that the glyph detonation worked, and felt the same flicker of surprise — *oh. Oh, that worked.*
source_quote: I understood it. I felt the same flicker of it, the half-second of *oh. Oh, that worked.*

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator noted that Zalthir and Thorin were unsinged after Daz’s Fireball, as planned.
source_quote: I note that Zalthir is unsinged. I note that Thorin is unsinged.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator observed that the fungus was still standing, anchoring the battlefield, and that the fight was far from over.
source_quote: The fungus was still standing. The fight was far from over.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator takes notes either way, whether Bahamut is watching or not.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been watching. I took notes either way.
